packet.description_seed: A body found in New South Wales is thought to be that of a man wanted over a triple murder.

clean_source_blocks.text: A body found in New South Wales is thought to be that of a man wanted over the murder of three people in a small Australian town in January. Julian Ingram was on bail for domestic violence offences at the time of the killings of his pregnant ex-partner Sophie Quinn, her friend and her aunt in Lake Cargelligo, about 450km (280mi) west of Sydney. All were shot. Police said on Monday that a man's body, understood to be Ingram, was discovered beside an abandoned ute 50km (31mi) north-west of where the murders happened. He was last seen on January 22 and police say the body appears to have been there "for some time". It was discovered by wildlife officers out eradicating feral pests.
A body found in New South Wales is thought to be that of a man wanted over a triple murder.

Suspected triple-murderer Julian Ingram was on the run since the fatal shootings in late January. (Supplied: NSW Police) A body found in NSW's Central West is believed to be that of alleged triple murderer Julian Ingram. The 37-year-old has been on the run since January 22 when three people were shot dead in Lake Cargelligo. Police said the discovery of the body would bring "closure" and "relief" to the town. NSW Police believe a body found in the state's Central West is that of alleged triple murderer Julian Ingram. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article contains names and images of Indigenous people who have died used with permission from the family.

Western Region Commander, Assistant Commissioner Andrew Holland, has confirmed the ute was the same vehicle the wanted man was seen driving from the scene. "Next to this vehicle, police have also located a male body in a very decomposed state," he said. "Next to this body is a firearm and at this point believe the person laying next to the vehicle could be Julian Ingram, but he's yet to be formally identified. "We believe that the identification at the scene, the clothing that the deceased is wearing, would lead us to believe that it is him." Assistant Commissioner Holland said it was "unclear" whether police had previously searched the area as part of the massive manhunt for the alleged killer.

[Lähde: BBC World]
A body found in New South Wales is thought to be that of a man wanted over the murder of three people in a small Australian town in January.

Julian Ingram was on bail for domestic violence offences at the time of the killings of his pregnant ex-partner Sophie Quinn, her friend and her aunt in Lake Cargelligo, about 450km (280mi) west of Sydney. All were shot.

Police said on Monday that a man's body, understood to be Ingram, was discovered beside an abandoned ute 50km (31mi) north-west of where the murders happened.

He was last seen on January 22 and police say the body appears to have been there "for some time".

It was discovered by wildlife officers out eradicating feral pests.

Assistant commissioner Andrew Holland told reporters they have confirmed the vehicle they found was the one driven by Ingram.

"We believe that the identification at the scene, the clothing that the deceased is wearing, would lead us to believe that it is him," Holland said, ABC reported.

On 22 January, Ingram allegedly shot dead his former partner Sophie Quinn, her friend and a relative of Quinn. Quinn was reportedly seven-months pregnant and was due to give birth to a son in March.

The shootings also seriously injured a 19-year-old man, who has since been released from hospital, according to the police.

Shortly after the shootings, authorities deployed around 100 officers to search for Ingram.

Holland said at the time that Ingram, an employee of the local council, had extensive local knowledge and could "maintain an extended period in the local area without being detected.

Lake Cargelligo is located in the centre of New South Wales and has a population of about 1,500 people.

On Monday, Holland said the discovery of what they believed to be Ingram's body "brings closure to this investigation" and "gives some solace to the town so they can relax".

payload.title: Poliisi löysi ruumiin, jonka uskotaan olevan Australian kolmoissurmista etsitty mies
payload.summary: New South Walesissa löydetyn ruumiin uskotaan olevan Julian Ingram, jota etsittiin kolmen ihmisen ampumisesta Lake Cargelligossa tammikuussa. Virallinen tunnistaminen on vielä kesken.
payload.content:
New South Walesin poliisi uskoo löytäneensä ruumiin, joka voi olla tammikuussa tapahtuneista kolmoissurmista etsitty Julian Ingram. Kolme ihmistä ammuttiin kuoliaaksi Lake Cargelligon pienessä kaupungissa, noin 450 kilometriä Sydneystä länteen. Poliisin mukaan ruumis löytyi hylätyn avolava-auton vierestä noin 50 kilometriä luoteeseen tapahtumapaikasta, mutta henkilöllisyyttä ei ole vielä vahvistettu virallisesti.

## Ruumis löytyi hylätyn ajoneuvon vierestä

Poliisin mukaan miesruumis löydettiin New South Walesin keskiosista ajoneuvon läheltä. Western Region Commanderin apulaiskomissaari Andrew Holland kertoi, että avolava-auto oli sama ajoneuvo, jolla etsityn miehen oli nähty poistuvan surmapaikalta. Ruumiin vierestä löytyi myös ampuma-ase.

Viranomaisten mukaan ruumis oli pitkälle maatunut. Hollandin mukaan paikalta tehdyt havainnot, mukaan lukien vainajan vaatetus, viittaavat siihen, että kyseessä voi olla 37-vuotias Julian Ingram. Poliisi on kuitenkin korostanut, että muodollinen tunnistaminen on yhä kesken.

Ruumiin löysivät villieläinviranomaiset, jotka olivat alueella hävittämässä haitallisina pidettyjä villiintyneitä eläimiä. Poliisin mukaan ruumis näyttää olleen löytöpaikalla jo jonkin aikaa. Holland sanoi myös, ettei ole selvää, oliko poliisi aiemmin etsinyt juuri tältä alueelta osana laajaa etsintää.

## Ingramia etsittiin tammikuun ampumisten jälkeen

Ingram oli ollut karkuteillä 22. tammikuuta lähtien. Tuolloin kolme ihmistä ammuttiin kuoliaaksi Lake Cargelligossa. Uhrien joukossa olivat hänen raskaana ollut entinen puolisonsa Sophie Quinn sekä Quinnin ystävä ja täti.

Lähdetietojen mukaan Ingram oli tapahtumahetkellä vapaana takuita vastaan perheväkivaltaan liittyvistä rikosepäilyistä. Ampumisten jälkeen poliisi käynnisti laajan etsintäoperaation, joka jatkui kuukausia ja keskittyi New South Walesin keskiosiin.

## Poliisi puhuu helpotuksesta yhteisölle

New South Walesin poliisi arvioi, että löytö voi tuoda Lake Cargelligon yhteisölle helpotusta ja jonkinlaista päätöstä pitkään jatkuneeseen epävarmuuteen. Samalla tapaus ei ole vielä päättynyt viranomaisten näkökulmasta: seuraavaksi keskeistä on ruumiin virallinen tunnistaminen sekä löytöpaikan ja olosuhteiden tarkempi selvittäminen.
